sec: Scrub typhus: agent, progression, features and treatment; malaria life cycle

items.q: What is the infectious agent of scrub typhus, as printed?
Disease progression in scrub typhus — match — 1) Renal lesion 2) Immunological phase … A) Micro-infarcts in kidney with ATN and a thrombotic microangiopathic pattern B) No immunological phase
items.exp: 'micro infarct in kidney (ATN + Thrombotic microangiopathic pattern)' and 'No immunological phase'. (Book p1058)

items.q: What is printed as the characteristic feature of scrub typhus?
Judge the scrub typhus block: I The presentation resembles leptospirosis. II Lymphadenopathy appears at the end of one week.
items.exp: '· Similar presentation as leptospirosis' and 'Lymphadenopathy at the end of one week'. (Book p1058)

items.q: Untreated scrub typhus — match the feature to its timing/type — 1) CNS involvement 2) Hearing 3) Eye movements … A) Sensorineural deafness, reversible B) Opsoclonus and myoclonus C) Within one week
items.exp: 'If untreated → CNS involvement (within one week) : Sensorineural deafness (Reversible), Opsoclonus, myoclonus'. (Book p1058)

items.q: What doxycycline regimen is printed for scrub typhus?
What azithromycin regimen is printed as the alternative for scrub typhus?
Judge the scrub typhus treatment: I Doxycycline 100 mg twice daily for 7 days. II Azithromycin 500 mg once daily for 5 days is the alternative.
items.exp: Both regimens are printed on the scrap typhus block. (Book p1058)

items.q: Malaria life cycle — match — 1) Infective form 2) Liver stage 3) Blood stage … A) Pre-erythrocytic schizogony B) Sporozoites C) Erythrocytic schizogony with merozoite release and RBC rupture
items.exp: 'Sporozoites (Infective form) → Via blood → Liver → Pre-erythrocytic schizogony → Released → merozoites → Rupture RBC's → Erythrocytic schizogony → Fever'. (Book p1058)

items.q: What is printed as the infective form in the malaria life cycle?
Which stage name is given to hepatic schizogony on this page?
Judge the malaria cycle: I Sporozoites reach the liver through the blood. II Fever coincides with erythrocytic schizogony and RBC rupture.
items.exp: Both statements follow the printed cycle ending in 'Erythrocytic schizogony → Fever'. (Book p1058)
